chunkIdsSha256Spec: sha256 over UTF-8 of the chunk ids: token ids in decimal joined by ',' within a chunk, chunks joined by ';'. Ids include [CLS]/[SEP] and exclude padding.
textRecipeSpec: kind 'literal' -> text as given; kind 'repeat' -> text concatenated 'times' times with no separator.

cases.name: short_single_chunk
cases.note: A short document: one unit, one chunk, sequence far below 512. Pins the dynamic padding width -- a port that always pads to 512 fails here.

textRecipe.text: The quarterly budget report sets out expenditure against each cost centre for the financial year. Total operating expenditure was 4.2 million, against an approved budget of 4.5 million, leaving an underspend of 300 thousand.

cases.name: boundary_just_under
cases.note: 504 content tokens: one token block still inside the 510-token budget, so it stays a single unit and a single chunk. The near miss on the boundary is the point.

textRecipe.text: The finance committee approved the departmental expenditure for the current quarter.

cases.name: boundary_overlap_carry
cases.note: 516 content tokens: one token over the budget, so the block descends to sentences and the second chunk is seeded with the 64-token carry-over. The narrowest test of the overlap there is.

textRecipe.text: The finance committee approved the departmental expenditure for the current quarter.

cases.name: three_chunks
cases.note: Around 1200 content tokens: three chunks, so the carry-over is applied twice and chunk lengths settle at the steady-state 510.

textRecipe.text: The finance committee approved the departmental expenditure for the current quarter.

cases.name: eight_chunks
cases.note: Around 3360 content tokens: eight chunks in one run() call, which is also more chunks than the recorded micro_batch_size of 8 leaves slack for -- the graph pools all of them into one document regardless.

textRecipe.text: The finance committee approved the departmental expenditure for the current quarter.

cases.name: min_final_chunk
cases.note: A 510-token block followed by a one-token block. Produces the SHORTEST final chunk the V6.2.01 geometry admits: 64 carried tokens plus one. See the README on why the min_tokens tail extension cannot fire.

cases.name: blank_line_blocks
cases.note: Sixty blank-line-separated blocks. Every unit boundary is a BLOCK_PATTERN match, so chunks close between blocks and never inside one.

cases.name: unsplittable_long_line
cases.note: One line, no newline and no sentence-ending punctuation: block split and sentence split both return a single part, so the chunker descends to the hard split of the token ids. Also forces the carried head to be TRIMMED from the left, because each unit is exactly a full budget wide.

cases.name: punctuation_and_numbers
cases.note: Digits, decimals, currency and bracketed references. WordPiece fragments these heavily, so a port with a hand-rolled tokenizer diverges here first.
